home.subtext: Your data will help make a better future of work for yourself and other drivers.
home.section1.title: Rideshare platforms conceal important information from drivers
home.section1.description: Platforms purposefully hide the full cost of rides to prevent drivers from organizing for better pay. Our data shows that Uber can take over 80% of fares.
home.section2.title: Your data supports important labor movements nationwide
home.section2.subsection1.title: Supporting deactivated drivers
home.section2.subsection1.description: Labor unions are using System to help deactivated drivers recover lost wages.
home.section2.subsection2.title: Investigating algorithmic wage discrimination
home.section2.subsection2.description: System data is helping national organizations like EDL to investigate wether workers can get unequal pay for similar work.
home.section2.subsection3.title: Tracking changes in pay over time
home.section2.subsection3.description: Labor unions are using System to track changes in the quality of work in the rideshare and food industry.

driver.survey.takeinfo.a-take-rate-is-th: A take rate is the share of a fare, excluding tips, that the platform keeps as fees.
driver.survey.takeinfo.we-calculate-your: We average take rate on rideshare trips from your linked accounts over the past six months when fare and fee fields are present. In our data this is reliable mainly for Uber Driver trips. Lyft take rate is not supported here—driver-facing history often lacks rider-paid totals or a usable fee breakdown—so we do not show a separate Lyft figure. If you also drive for Lyft or other platforms, incomplete fee data on those trips can skew the average you see; read the percentage mainly as a guide to your Uber activity.
